cues.zh: 有个 Portofino Inn，由 Mary Davis 经营，她算是个赛车迷，会在那儿办派对之类的。所以那正好是个合适的海岸

I ended up with a Ferrari Daytona with Dan Gurney, my old teammate. Not all that much preparation with respect to the way you would normally prepare a car for a cannonball, but they set a time of thirty five hours and fifty four minutes, which was, of course, the new record.
cues.zh: 你可能会觉得，在一群汽车爱好者中提出这样的比赛，会有成百上千辆车报名。但实际上，第一届大概只有十几辆车参赛。我最后和老队友 Dan Gurney 开着一辆 Ferrari Daytona 参赛。我们没有像准备普通横跨美国耐力赛那样做多少准备，但他们跑出了 35 小时 54 分钟，当然，这也成了新的纪录。

cues.en: Now that Ralph Nader, who proudly proclaims that he seldom drives himself, has become the principal spokesman for America's drivers, we, as a group of people who like automobiles,
cues.zh: 既然 Ralph Nader 这位自称很少开车的家伙，已经成了全美司机的头号代言人，那我们这群热爱汽车的人，

cues.zh: 限速往好里说是虚伪，

cues.zh: 往坏里说就是站不住脚。所以人们只能把它当成一种现实来接受，但绝不能奉为圭臬。毕竟，要是连警察自己都不遵守——相信我，他们确实不遵守——那我们凭什么要遵守？

cues.en: Despite the economic squeeze on the European show circuit, this year's display at Geneva had its fair share of new and noteworthy cars. The Italian makes were most impressive.
cues.zh: 尽管欧洲车展巡回受到了经济下行的挤压，但今年日内瓦车展上依旧不乏亮眼的新车。其中意大利品牌最为惊艳。

cues.en: you have the Geneva Auto Show. The Lamborghini Countach was unveiled.
cues.zh: 那是日内瓦车展。Lamborghini Countach 惊艳亮相。

cues.en: It shocked the world.
cues.zh: 它震撼了全世界。

cues.en: Before it had been released to the public, you had Bob Wallace and you had one of the other engineers that was going to see the car in Bruton for the first time. Apparently, the lights were off in the room and security was letting them in to come see the car. And when someone turned on the lights, the security guard said, Countach, which essentially meant holy shit.
cues.zh: 在它向公众发布之前，Bob Wallace 和另一位工程师正准备在 Bruton 第一次见识这辆车。据说当时房间里的灯是关着的，保安放他们进去看车。当有人把灯打开时，保安脱口而出一句“Countach”，意思基本上就是“卧槽”。

cues.en: The Countach is radical. You look at it and go, my god, this is a spaceship. It's a different approach. Looking back, the beauty of Lamborghini was, you know, Ferrari as a manufacturer that was building cars for a purpose. It was building production cars to fund racing,
cues.zh: Countach 很激进。你看着它就会想：天哪，这简直是艘太空船。它采用了截然不同的设计思路。回头看，Lamborghini 的魅力在于，Ferrari 是一家为特定目的造车的制造商。它造量产车来资助赛车项目，

cues.en: and the same with Porsche. Lamborghini was completely opposite. Lamborghini was not a brand that has its history in racing, and that's been a criticism at times, but that's not always what road cars are about. Great race cars make terrible road cars, and usually great road cars make terrible race cars. People don't build race cars to look awesome,
cues.zh: Porsche 也是如此。Lamborghini 则完全相反。Lamborghini 的品牌历史并非建立在赛车之上，这一点有时会受到批评，但公路车并不总是为了赛车而造。出色的赛车往往不适合上路，而出色的公路车通常也不适合比赛。人们造赛车可不是为了让它看起来很酷，

cues.en: and that's what this was.
cues.zh: 而这辆车就是这样。

cues.en: When Fluccio came up with this concept of having something different, this was all about the high life. And back in the day, there weren't many exotic vehicles, you think about it. There were only a few. Frutio Lamborghini was a entrepreneur
cues.zh: 当 Ferruccio 提出这种与众不同的构想时，这完全关乎上流社会的生活方式。回想当年，其实并没有多少超级跑车，数量屈指可数。Ferruccio Lamborghini 当时是一位

cues.en: and industrialist in Italy. He had a tractor company, amongst many other companies. He had an air conditioning company as well and other things. He at the time actually had a two fifty GT Ferrari,
cues.zh: 意大利的企业家兼实业家。在众多产业中，他拥有一家拖拉机公司，还做过空调公司等等。那时他正好有一辆 Ferrari 250 GT，

cues.en: and he was basically complaining about the clutch and complaining about other issues with the car. The story goes that he'd went to go complain to Enzo Ferrari and say, hey, maybe we should change this or do this. And Ferrari told him to basically get out of his office. He said, you know, you stick to building tractors and, you know, I'll stick to building cars.
cues.zh: 他总在抱怨那辆车的离合器以及其他各种毛病。据说他跑去找 Enzo Ferrari 抱怨，说“嘿，也许咱们该改改这里，或者这么做”。而 Ferrari 基本上就是叫他滚出办公室，说“你管好你造拖拉机的事，造车的事留给我”。

cues.en: And I think Ferruccio was, you know, the type of character that wasn't gonna take no and decided that he was gonna go build a better car.
cues.zh: 我觉得 Ferruccio 就是那种不肯认输的人，他决定要造一辆更好的车。

cues.en: First prototype was built in 1963.
cues.zh: 第一辆原型车造于1963年。

cues.en: And then imagine by 1964,
cues.zh: 然后想象一下，到1964年，

cues.en: 1965, they had a production car, which is the three fifty GT.
cues.zh: 1965年，他们就有了量产车，也就是350 GT。

cues.en: The three fifty GT was essentially Frutcho's answer to the two fifty GT and the other GT cars produced by Ferrari, V12 front engine. And if you look at the three fifty GT, the details are outstanding. I mean, the fit and finish and and the gauges and all these different things. To this day, people walk in our showroom, and if we have a GT, they go right to the car.
cues.zh: 350 GT 本质上就是 Frutcho 对250 GT以及法拉利生产的其他GT车型的回应——V12前置发动机。如果你仔细看350 GT，细节非常出色。我是说，装配和涂装、仪表盘，还有所有这些不同的东西。直到今天，人们走进我们的展厅，如果我们有一辆GT，他们会直奔那辆车。

cues.en: The beauty of what Frutcho did was he went to the best of the best. I mean, if you go down the list of the engineers that have worked in Lamborghini during those early days, you have Bizzarini, Gallara, have Stanzani, know, on and on and on. And he allowed great teams to do incredible work. There was no, we shouldn't do that or no. It was really, you know, forward thinking. You look at that evolution. So you have the three fifty GT as the first production car.
cues.zh: Frutcho 的做法很妙，他找来的都是顶尖人才。你看看早期在兰博基尼工作的工程师名单：有 Bizzarini、Gallara、Stanzani，等等等等。他让优秀的团队做出了惊人的成果。他从不说“这事不能做”。他的想法真的很超前。看看这段发展历程：第一款量产车是 350 GT。

cues.en: And then within, let's call it a year or two, you have the launch of the Mura.
cues.zh: 然后大概也就一两年的时间，Miura 就发布了。

cues.en: There was nothing like it as a production car, a transverse mid engine that was beautiful.
cues.zh: 作为量产车，它绝对是绝无仅有的，横置中置引擎，而且美轮美奂。

cues.en: Fruciel Lamborghini really set a bold statement as a boutique supercar manufacturer. And at that time, the concept had not been described yet. What those two cars as his first production cars?
cues.zh: Ferruccio Lamborghini 彻底立下了精品超跑厂商的鲜明旗帜，而当时甚至连超跑的概念都还没成型。凭借这两款车作为他的首批开山之作，

cues.en: In many ways, a Lamborghini is a caricature of a normal car. Yes. It has an engine, but it's got 12 cylinders. It's naturally aspirated. Yes. It has a transmission, but it's a gated manual gearbox that gives you an unmistakable
cues.zh: 在很多方面，Lamborghini 就像是普通汽车的夸张化身。没错，它有引擎，但那是 V12，还是自然吸气。没错，它有变速箱，但那是手感鲜明的开放式金属挡槽手动变速箱，

cues.en: and totally distinct driving characteristic.
cues.zh: 能带给你绝无仅有、独一无二的驾驶体验。

cues.en: Yes. People spent time trying to make it visually appealing, but instead of just doing it to be good enough, they took it to the moon and back to make sure that anybody who ever saw it would never forget. These cars are a labor of love to the brand and to the engineers and the designers that are behind them. Remember, this was all handmade in Bologna.
cues.zh: 是的。人们花时间让它在外观上吸引人，但他们不只是做到够好就行，而是不惜一切做到极致，确保任何见过它的人都永远忘不了。这些车是對品牌、对背后的工程师和设计师倾注心血的结晶。记住，这一切都是在博洛尼亚手工打造的。

cues.en: They were in a production facility of craftsman from the engine bits to machining parts. Nothing left that facility. You saw artisans that were pounding the aluminum panels. The detail that goes into putting the cars together and building that engine, it was incredible.
cues.zh: 他们身处一个工匠云集的生产设施中，从发动机部件到机加工零件，什么都离不开那个设施。你能看到工匠们在敲打铝板。组装这些车、打造那台发动机所投入的细节，简直令人难以置信。

cues.en: How do you follow an act like a Miura? Just probably the most beautiful car ever produced. When a car like a Lamborghini Countach was built, you're not necessarily looking to say, Hey, how do we make this most comfortable? How many golf clubs can we put in it? When you build a car like that, the first priority is always the experience.
cues.zh: 想要超越 Miura 这样的车型，该怎么做？它大概是有史以来最美的汽车。打造 Lamborghini Countach 这样的车时，你考虑的未必是：“怎么才能让它最舒适？能装下多少根高尔夫球杆？”造这样的车，第一要务始终是驾乘体验。

cues.en: And not just the experience of the driver, but anyone who comes into contact with the car. You're talking about something that stirs the emotions and excites the senses in ways that most things never could.
cues.zh: 而且不只是驾驶者的体验，还有每个接触到这辆车的人的体验。它能触动情感、点燃感官，带来的感受是大多数事物都无法比拟的。

cues.en: The Countach was developed over many years. Bertone design, that was the design house that was responsible for the Countach body. But Marcello Gandini is the person who designed it.
cues.zh: Countach 的研发历经了许多年。负责设计 Countach 车身的是 Bertone 设计工作室。但真正的操刀设计师是 Marcello Gandini。

cues.en: Bob Wallace was the original test driver, really developed the Countach. You can see him driving this original LP 500,
cues.zh: Bob Wallace 是最早的测试车手，Countach 的实际调校很大程度上出自他手。你可以看到他正在驾驶这台最初的 LP 500，

cues.en: which was the prototype car. That was eventually developed into the first LP 400,
cues.zh: 也就是那辆原型车。它最终演变成了第一款 LP 400，

cues.en: Parascopio. The original LP400s
cues.zh: 即 Parascopio。最初的 LP 400

cues.en: were referred to as Parascopio cars. And the reason why is that there was this indent in the roof and the rearview mirror came up the top and you could see it through the indent.
cues.zh: 被称为“潜望镜”（Parascopio）版。之所以这么叫，是因为车顶有一个凹槽，后视镜从顶部升起，你可以透过这个凹槽看到后方。

cues.en: Just taking a step back at the vehicle and looking at how dramatic it was, what other vehicle can you and I think about in the seventies that had that type of design? Nothing.
cues.zh: 退一步看这辆车，看看它有多惊艳，七十年代你能想到还有哪款车有这种设计？没有了。

cues.en: The concept of Lamborghini
cues.zh: 兰博基尼的理念

cues.en: making a bold statement to Enzo Ferrari and how the company was started almost like an f u to, you know, society. It's like, I can do this and I will.
cues.zh: 向恩佐·法拉利发出大胆宣言，公司创立几乎像是对社会的一种叫板。就像在说，我能做到，而且我一定会做。

cues.en: And I think that DNA has stuck with Lamborghini from the Countach.
cues.zh: 我认为这种DNA从Countach开始就一直留在兰博基尼身上。

cues.en: This design is the classic wedge. It's 50 years old this year. All of these decades later, you can still park that car in any lot, and it still looks futuristic. No matter how old it gets, it just seems to be timeless to where it never seems like an older design. The ingenuity underneath is really what's out of this world for that time. It's chassis. The design of all these tubular components that create almost like a birdcage. I think you could probably hang a chassis at a modern museum and people would say, wow, that's incredible. The Countach, when it came out in the seventies, it set the bar, and it's always been the one that people just said, this is the most amazing car anyone has ever made.
cues.zh: 这种设计就是经典的楔形车身。今年它已经 50 岁了。几十年过去了，你把这辆车停在哪个停车场里，它看起来依然充满未来感。无论车龄有多大，它的设计似乎始终不过时，从来不会让人觉得老旧。当年它底下那些巧妙的设计，才是真正令人惊叹的地方。它的底盘由许多管状部件构成，整体看起来就像一个鸟笼。我觉得把这样的底盘挂在现代美术馆里，人们大概都会惊叹：太不可思议了。Countach 在 70 年代问世时就树立了标杆。从那以后，人们一直觉得它是有史以来最惊艳的汽车。

cues.en: Not just aesthetically
cues.zh: 不仅是在外观上

cues.en: was it wild with the doors that went up. I mean, you're talking about a V 12 engine that at the time was producing almost 400 horsepower. Later variants imagine
cues.zh: 靠着剪刀门野性十足。我是说，那可是一台在当时能输出近 400 匹马力的 V12 发动机。后期的版本你想想

cues.en: carbureted almost 500 horsepower
cues.zh: 靠化油器就能压榨出近 500 匹马力，

cues.en: in a car that could almost break 200 miles per hour.
cues.zh: 而且这辆车的极速几乎能突破 200 英里每小时。

cues.en: The incredible feeling of stability and purpose and the sheer precision of a car that has no other reason for existence than to spear down the road as far and as fast as possible. That feeling is so strong in the Countach,
cues.zh: 那种难以置信的稳定性、纯粹的目标感，以及极致的精准度——这辆车存在的唯一意义，就是尽可能风驰电掣地在路上狂飙。这种感觉在 Countach 身上是如此强烈，

cues.en: it can take your breath away.
cues.zh: 甚至能让你屏住呼吸。

cues.zh: Rock Hates 创下了纪录。但当你创下这样的纪录时，显然它就是大家要挑战的目标。而到了72年，他们遇到了恶劣天气，所以在第二轮竞技跑中没人能打破它。

cues.en: I wrote a note to Brock Hates and said, If you ever run this again, invite me. Brock was very selective in who he would allow and how that was all going to be organized. Everybody was screened. You had to have somebody vouch for you. You had to have certain insurance coverage.
cues.zh: 我给 Brock Hates 写了张便条，说，如果你再办这个比赛，邀请我。Brock 对允许谁参加以及整个组织方式非常挑剔。每个人都要经过筛选。你得有人为你担保。你得有特定的保险。

cues.en: You had to have a skill set as a driver. If somebody was too gung ho,
cues.zh: 你得具备驾驶员的技能。如果有人太过冲动，

cues.en: they didn't qualify. We took no chance. We never scared or endangered anyone else. We wanted to be careful. We didn't want to embarrass Brock, right? Yeah. These are capable drivers in capable cars driving safely, and they were. And so is that gonna carry the day? Is that gonna compel policy? No. But it made it a little bit more redemptive.
cues.zh: 那就不符合资格。我们不冒险，绝不会吓到或危及其他人。我们想谨慎一些，也不想让 Brock 难堪，对吧？是啊。这些驾驶员技术过硬，开的车也性能可靠，而且他们确实安全驾驶了。这样能左右局势吗？能推动政策吗？不能。但至少让这件事多了些积极意义。

cues.zh: 英里的时速横穿全国了吗？当然不行。驾驶是一种社会责任，必须以谨慎和理智来衡量。“加农炮贝克”靠的是沉稳

cues.zh: 与顺畅。

cues.zh: 哦，一辆华丽的法拉利。我们没那么充分的准备。我们连雷达探测器都没有，到纽约之前也没有任何行车灯。我们确实有个燃料电池。他有这辆白色Dino，装了个燃料电池，结果漏油了

cues.zh: 每次你看到有人

cues.en: do it, you'd learn how they did it. And throughout all that, they're able to devise their own way to just up the ante a bit. And so every time you see better prepared cars, better lighting, better electronics, Not only did they have CB radios, which were really, really useful because the truckers were also trying to outsmart the cops, but you also had rudimentary police scanners, and you'd also have some radar detectors, fuzzbusters, and things like that that worked okay. You'd also have kill switches for your lights, maybe both sets of lights, and certainly different ways to disguise the car, different
cues.zh: 这么干，就能学到他们是怎么做的。而在这一过程中，他们还能想出自己的办法，再把难度提高一点。所以每次你看到准备得更充分的车、更好的灯光和电子设备，他们不仅有民用波段电台——这东西特别有用，因为卡车司机也在想办法瞒过警察——还有简易的警用无线电扫描仪、雷达探测器、Fuzzbuster 之类的设备，效果都还不错。他们还会给车灯装断电开关，也许前后两组灯都有；当然，也会用不同的方法伪装车辆，用不同的
